purpose: The file access policy daemon itself

sections.title: Command-line flags
sections.code:
fapolicyd --debug              # Foreground; print every access decision to stderr
fapolicyd --debug-deny         # Foreground; print only denied decisions to stderr
fapolicyd --permissive         # Log decisions but allow everything (testing)
fapolicyd --no-details         # Omit file/process names from the shutdown usage report

sections.title: Service management
sections.code:
systemctl status fapolicyd
systemctl enable --now fapolicyd     # RHEL-09-433015: fapolicy module must be enabled
systemctl restart fapolicyd

sections.title: Signals
sections.code:
kill -TERM $(pidof fapolicyd)   # Stop cleanly, writing the usage report first
kill -HUP  $(pidof fapolicyd)   # Reload the trust database
kill -USR1 $(pidof fapolicyd)   # Dump internal statistics to /var/run/fapolicyd.state

sections.title: Investigating denials
sections.code:
ausearch --start today -m fanotify -i    # Denials logged as FANOTIFY audit events
journalctl -u fapolicyd                  # Daemon's own log (syslog/journal)
tail -f /var/log/fapolicyd-access.log    # do_stat_report output on shutdown

notes: Never attach ptrace (debugger/strace) to fapolicyd: it delivers an unblockable SIGSTOP, and since core library access itself depends on fapolicyd's approval, this can deadlock the system.

purpose: Manage the trust database, inspect rules, and check daemon health

sections.title: Trust database
sections.code:
fapolicyd-cli --file add /path/to/binary       # Add a file to the trust database
fapolicyd-cli --file delete /path/to/binary    # Remove a file from the trust database
fapolicyd-cli --file update /path/to/binary    # Refresh a file's trust database entry
fapolicyd-cli --update                         # Notify the running daemon to reload the trust database
fapolicyd-cli --delete-db                      # Delete the trust database (recovery from corruption)
fapolicyd-cli --dump-db                        # Dump trust source, path, size, and SHA256 for every entry

sections.title: Rules & file types
sections.code:
fapolicyd-cli --list                    # List the compiled rules file with rule numbers
fapolicyd-cli --ftype /path/to/file     # Print the MIME type fapolicyd assigns this file
fapolicyd-cli --trust-file myapp.trust  # Operate on one named file inside /etc/fapolicyd/trust.d/

sections.title: Health & diagnostics
sections.code:
fapolicyd-cli --check-config     # Validate fapolicyd.conf syntax
fapolicyd-cli --check-trustdb    # Compare the trust database against the files on disk
fapolicyd-cli --check-path       # Check $PATH entries against the trust database
fapolicyd-cli --check-watch_fs   # Compare mounted filesystems against the watch_fs config
fapolicyd-cli --check-status     # Dump the daemon's health/configuration state
fapolicyd-cli --check-metrics    # Dump the daemon's internal performance statistics
